# NanoId

Short, URL-safe, unpredictable identifiers in the Nano ID format.

## Installation

Add `NanoId` to the `[Dependencies]` table of your package's `Rux.toml`:

```toml
[Dependencies]
NanoId = { Namespace = "Rux", Version = "0.1.0" }
```

Standard packages are declared by hand: the registry does not serve them, so `rux add Rux/NanoId` cannot add them.

## Dependencies

- [`Core`](/docs/api/core) 0.1.0
- [`Entropy`](/docs/api/entropy) 0.1.0
- [`Memory`](/docs/api/memory) 0.1.0
- [`Text`](/docs/api/text) 0.1.0

## Guide

### What it provides

| Module                                          | Covers                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| [`NanoId`](/docs/api/nanoid/nano-id)            | the [`NanoId`](/docs/api/nanoid/nano-id) value: [`Generate`](/docs/api/nanoid/nano-id#generate), [`Parse`](/docs/api/nanoid/nano-id#parse), [`Text`](/docs/api/nanoid/nano-id#text), [`Equals`](/docs/api/nanoid/nano-id#equals), [`Compare`](/docs/api/nanoid/nano-id#compare), `Display` and `Debug` |
| [`Generate`](/docs/api/nanoid/nano-id#generate) | [`GenerateNanoId`](/docs/api/nanoid/generate#generate-nano-id) and [`GenerateNanoIdFrom`](/docs/api/nanoid/generate#generate-nano-id-from), which fill a buffer of any length from any alphabet                                                                                                        |
| `Alphabet`                                      | [`NanoIdAlphabet`](/docs/api/nanoid/alphabet#nano-id-alphabet), [`NanoIdLength`](/docs/api/nanoid/alphabet#nano-id-length), [`NanoIdError`](/docs/api/nanoid/nano-id-error) and [`ValidateAlphabet`](/docs/api/nanoid/alphabet#validate-alphabet)                                                      |

The module names describe where each declaration comes from; they are not part of an import path.

### Example

```rux
import NanoId::{ GenerateNanoId, NanoId };

func NewSessionToken() -> bool {
    let id = NanoId::Generate() catch { else => return false };
    var code: char8[8];
    GenerateNanoId(code[..], "0123456789") catch { else => return false };
    return id.Text().length == 21;
}
```

### Design

A standard identifier is twenty-one characters from the sixty-four URL-safe characters `A`–`Z`, `a`–`z`, `0`–`9`, `_` and `-`, which is 126 random bits: more than a version 4 UUID carries, in fewer characters, and safe unescaped in a URL or a file name. [`NanoId`](/docs/api/nanoid/nano-id) holds one inline as a `Copy` value. [`GenerateNanoId`](/docs/api/nanoid/generate#generate-nano-id) fills a buffer of any length instead, from the default alphabet or a custom one.

Every character of the alphabet is equally likely at every position. Each character is a random byte masked down to the smallest power of two that covers the alphabet, and a masked value past the end of the alphabet is thrown away rather than folded back with a remainder, which would favour the first characters. A custom alphabet must have between two and 256 distinct ASCII characters; [`ValidateAlphabet`](/docs/api/nanoid/alphabet#validate-alphabet) says which rule it broke, before any entropy is spent.

Random bytes come from the operating system through `Rux/Entropy`. Generation fails rather than producing a predictable identifier when the system has none, and leaves the destination zeroized rather than holding the start of an identifier. [`GenerateNanoIdFrom`](/docs/api/nanoid/generate#generate-nano-id-from) takes any `EntropySource`, which is how a test gets reproducible identifiers. The default alphabet is listed in the reference implementation's order, so the same random bytes give the same identifier here as in other implementations.

[`Equals`](/docs/api/nanoid/nano-id#equals) compares every byte whatever it finds, so comparing a guessed identifier with a real one takes the same time however much of the guess was right.

## Index

### Types

| Name                                                               | Summary                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`NanoIdError`](/docs/api/nanoid/nano-id-error)                    | Why an identifier could not be generated.                                                                                  |
| [`NanoId`](/docs/api/nanoid/nano-id)                               | A Nano ID of the standard form: twenty-one characters from [`NanoIdAlphabet`](/docs/api/nanoid/alphabet#nano-id-alphabet). |
| [`NanoIdParseError`](/docs/api/nanoid/nano-id#nano-id-parse-error) | Why text could not be read as a standard Nano ID.                                                                          |

### Functions

| Name                                                                    | Summary                                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`ValidateAlphabet`](/docs/api/nanoid/alphabet#validate-alphabet)       | Checks that `alphabet` can be drawn from without bias.                                                          |
| [`GenerateNanoId`](/docs/api/nanoid/generate#generate-nano-id)          | Fills the whole of `into` with an identifier from the default alphabet, using the operating system's generator. |
| [`GenerateNanoIdFrom`](/docs/api/nanoid/generate#generate-nano-id-from) | Fills the whole of `into` with an identifier drawn from `alphabet`, using random bytes from `source`.           |
